arms.better: tm found the right implementation quickly and ultimately produced the correct one-line behavioral change. It spent two full 10-step attempts re-reading and re-searching without editing, then succeeded on a third attempt; tm stats reported 675,280 tokens for the run. Its stop message says to continue with `tm --resume S-1`/`S-2`, while `tm run` immediately dispatched another attempt, so the suggested recovery path and actual behavior were confusing and expensive. The third attempt also surfaced a `/tm/null` shell-start failure and a `couldn't find that` submission error before recovering, with little user-facing explanation. Better behavior would stop or resume the retained session after a no-progress limit, carry a focused continuation instruction into that retry, enforce a token ceiling, and expose command/submission errors alongside an actionable recovery step.
